clue.text: Don't accept rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone turning down a load of junk offered to them.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline something is to say no to it, and the noun means waste or garbage.

clue.text: Best ever monarch as part-time judge

parts.note: a record is the best performance ever achieved
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the monarch

explanation.surface: A praise of the finest king or queen who also sat on the bench now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: In England a RECORDER is a barrister or solicitor who sits as a judge part of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: In the English legal system this title names a lawyer appointed to sit as a judge on a part-time basis.

clue.text: Sporting conduct golfers try to stay within

parts.note: sporting behaviour is fair, in the sense of just play
a way is a manner of conduct or behaviour

explanation.surface: Good sportsmanship that golfers attempt to keep to.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers aim to keep their ball on the mown strip between tee and green, avoiding the rough.

clue.text: Small sculpture is French and protected by law

indicators.note: being protected by something means being enclosed inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a statute is a written law
et is French for 'and'

explanation.surface: A little carving that is French and covered by legal protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' puts ET inside STATUTE, after its first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurine is a small statue, a miniature sculptural figure.

clue.text: Old style for jumpers that's used by tailor

explanation.surface: A dated fashion for knitted pullovers worn by a tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The scissors was an old high-jump technique, the jumper kicking the legs over the bar one after the other; 'jumpers' hints at British knitted sweaters.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both an outdated high-jump technique and the cutting tool a tailor uses on cloth.

clue.text: Confuse me with erratic canal in Panama's region

indicators.note: to confuse things is to jumble them, so the letters that follow are mixed up

explanation.surface: A muddled-up waterway through Panama baffles the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confuse' rearranges ME, ERRATIC and CANAL together; 'erratic' is fodder here, not a second indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama lies at the southern end of the isthmus joining North and South America, the land bridge region.

clue.text: Clean area of stunted vegetation

explanation.surface: A tidy patch of low, scrappy bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: It means wash by rubbing hard, and also land covered with low bushes and stunted trees.

clue.text: Policeman's proposal about one caught

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: an offer is a proposal put forward
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A constable's suggestion concerning someone who has been arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I and C inside OFFER; the 's of 'Policeman's' is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A police constable is a police officer, the ordinary rank of the force.

clue.text: Locating one in trap set for criminals

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a sting is a police operation set up to catch crooks
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Finding a person caught in a police set-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Siting something is placing or positioning it in a particular spot.

clue.text: What's required of worker, proverbially patient?

definitions.text: What's required of worker, proverbially patient?

parts.words: What's required of worker, proverbially patient?
parts.note: the clue reads as a summary of a role's duties, and also as a portrait of the Bible's Job, whose patience is proverbial

explanation.surface: An outline of the duties expected of a long-suffering employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The patience of Job' is a proverb: the biblical Job endured his trials patiently, so 'patient' describes Job.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the document listing duties of a post, and also an account of the patient Biblical figure.

clue.text: Oriental area in Derby or Worcester, say?

definitions.text: Oriental area in Derby or Worcester, say?

parts.words: Oriental area in Derby or Worcester, say?
parts.note: Derby and Worcester are English towns famous for porcelain, so each is a porcelain town, and a city's Chinese quarter has the same name

explanation.surface: Asking whether an English county town has an East Asian quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Crown Derby and Royal Worcester are famous English porcelain makers; porcelain is called china.
explanation.definitionFit: A city's Chinese district is known by this name, here read as a town making china.

clue.text: Freshly equip extra man on field with it

parts.note: the referee is an additional person on the pitch beside the players
taken as written

explanation.surface: Kitting out the match official anew, along with something else.
explanation.definitionFit: To refit a ship or shop is to fit it out again with new equipment.

clue.text: Went back to start of tape about injury

definitions.text: Went back to start of tape

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a wound is an injury

explanation.surface: Someone returning to the beginning of a recording concerning an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooling a cassette back to its beginning is winding it again, in the past tense.

clue.text: One's boats are burned crossing this river

definitions.text: One's boats are burned crossing this river

parts.words: One's boats are burned crossing this river
parts.note: the clue joins two idioms for an irrevocable step, burning one's boats and crossing a certain Italian river, as Caesar did in 49 BC

explanation.surface: A river whose crossing means there is no going back.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar crossed this small river into Italy with his army, starting civil war; 'burning one's boats' also means committing beyond retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: This stream was the border Caesar crossed, and passing it now means a point of no return.

clue.text: Extremes of excitement concealing agony in country

indicators.note: concealing means holding something hidden inside, so the outer letters wrap round
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: gyp is informal British for pain, as in 'my back is giving me gyp'

explanation.surface: Thrills that mask suffering somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremes of' takes E and T, the first and last letters of 'excitement'; 'concealing' puts GYP between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a nation in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Royalist broken in lonely imprisonment

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A defeated monarchist locked away alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary confinement isolates a prisoner, and the word alone is slang for it.

clue.text: Specialized troops in unit ask for ceasefire

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Soldiers in a squad requesting a truce.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit assembled for a particular military operation is a specialised detachment of troops.

clue.text: English poet composed sonnet about American city

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the city
composed means put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: NY is New York

explanation.surface: A writer from England producing a fourteen-line poem about a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' turns SONNET into TENSON; 'about' wraps TEN-SON round NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate of England.

clue.text: Never in front, one's beaten by player

definitions.text: Never in front, one's beaten by player

parts.words: Never in front, one's beaten by player
parts.note: the clue sounds like a losing competitor, but describes a percussion instrument carried at a musician's flank, always beside the body and never before it

explanation.surface: Someone who never leads and is always beaten by their opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests a sports rival, but it is a musician; 'beaten' means struck with sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum worn at the flank in a marching band is named for that position.

clue.text: Raids or no raids, destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Raids or none, everything has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link word; only NO RAIDS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Making inroads is advancing into hostile territory, so the plural noun means incursions or attacks.

clue.text: For example, Victoria or Virginia, say

explanation.surface: Two women's names listed as examples of something spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a state of Australia, Virginia one of the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are named regions of a federation, and to declare something is to put it into words.

clue.text: Bewildered a lot, confused when fool's around

indicators.note: around means placed so as to enclose, so the fool wraps the jumble

parts.note: an ass is a fool; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of the words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Very puzzled while an idiot hangs about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' turns A LOT into TALO; 'around' puts A and SS either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stumped or perplexed is being unsure what to do.

clue.text: Joker in school gets rod for punishment

indicators.note: in places the joker inside school's abbreviation

parts.note: a wit is a clever joker

explanation.surface: A class clown at school earns a caning.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin flexible stick used for beating is called by this name.

clue.text: Move boat back to vessel for service

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: to row is to move a boat with oars
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: Rowing a small craft back to a larger one for a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious service is an act of devotion and praise.

clue.text: Short vacation time for composer

parts.note: hols is British short form of holidays

explanation.surface: A brief holiday is when a composer can relax.
explanation.walkthrough: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was an English composer best known for The Planets suite.

clue.text: Chorus lines monk kept in check

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the monk is placed within check

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
Fra is the title of an Italian friar or monk

explanation.surface: A singer's lines held back by a restraining monk.
explanation.definitionFit: The repeated verse of a song, sung after each stanza, is its chorus.

clue.text: Little time left to catch coarse fish with net

indicators.note: to catch means to hold inside, so these letters enclose the next

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
raw means coarse or crude

explanation.surface: An angler short of time trying for rough fish with a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coarse fish' is a British angling term for freshwater fish; here 'coarse' only means RAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Trawling is fishing by dragging a large net behind a boat.

clue.text: Run up debts, without any interest

parts.note: to incur debts is to run them up
IOUs are written notes of debt

explanation.surface: Building up debts but paying no interest on them.
explanation.definitionFit: An incurious person lacks curiosity, showing no desire to know more.

clue.text: Dithering, scrambling in haste, with little time

indicators.note: scrambling means jumbling up, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Wavering while hurrying with only moments to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wavering or undecided shows reluctance to act.

clue.text: For every child is a human being

parts.note: per means for each
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Each child counts as an individual.
explanation.definitionFit: An individual human is a person, someone rather than something.
